{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-pa-c","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"c93d08346c960f1feb4ef4c689a547b302ce5f91521d5ed1dea4c69b183af31a","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-pa-class-c:lineage:52","source_registry_sha256":"643bc755bc144bbb64c82e5b21691c27918519b2f96f9b0ff96b63899c04fddb","source_liveness_sha256":"d125293461efac0b369397a252e58fe1686ca24cdc89a306e2ea205c1feddb7c"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Sharing the road and work zones","heading":"C2 — Sharing the road and work zones","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — Sharing the road and work zones

FACT_ID: sec12-R01 | anchor: A05
Treat oversized loads like trucks and use extra caution when pilot vehicles with warning signs and lights appear. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec12-R02 | anchor: A05
An oversized load may cross a lane line to avoid roadside obstructions because of its width. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec12-R03 | anchor: A05
Never cross close behind a truck preparing to reverse into a loading area. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec12-R04 | anchor: A05
On a clear dry road at 65 mph, a loaded truck with good tires and adjusted brakes needs at least 600 feet to stop, compared with 400 feet for a passenger vehicle. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec12-R05 | anchor: A05
Avoid entering or changing lanes immediately in front of a large vehicle because its stopping distance is longer. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec12-R06 | anchor: A05
Escape ramps on long descents are reserved for large vehicles out of control or unable to stop through brake failure. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec12-R07 | anchor: A05
Do not park or stop near an escape ramp. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec12-R08 | anchor: A05
Use the same road-sharing precautions around buses as around trucks. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec12-R09 | anchor: A05
A school bus flashes amber lights as it prepares to stop. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec12-R10 | anchor: A05
Except from the opposite side of a physically divided highway, stop at least ten feet from a stopped school bus showing red flashers and an extended stop arm, whether following, meeting on its roadway or approaching its intersection. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec12-R11 | anchor: A05
Stay stopped for the school bus until its red flashers cease, its arm retracts and the children reach safety. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec12-R12 | anchor: A05
Opposite-direction traffic beyond a physical highway divider need not stop for the school bus but should slow and proceed cautiously. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec12-R13 | anchor: A05
An unlawful failure to stop for a bus with red flashers and an extended arm carries a sixty-day license suspension, five points and a fine. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec12-R14 | anchor: A06
For an emergency vehicle approaching from any direction with a siren or flashing red or red-and-blue lights, pull parallel to the curb or road edge and stop clear of intersections. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec12-R15 | anchor: A06
On a one-way road, move to the nearest roadside and stop for an approaching emergency vehicle. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec12-R16 | anchor: A06
Resume after the emergency vehicle passes, remain at least 500 feet behind it and check for another responder. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec12-R17 | anchor: A06
During emergencies, follow directions from uniformed officers, sheriffs, constables or properly attired responders including fire police. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec12-R18 | anchor: A06
Move into a nonadjacent lane when approaching an emergency-response area or marked disabled vehicle. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec12-R19 | anchor: A06
If traffic or other conditions prevent moving over, reduce speed at least twenty mph below the posted limit. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec12-R20 | anchor: A06
Road workers and emergency responders may report Move Over violations even without police present, and police may issue citations from those reports. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec12-R21 | anchor: A06
The handbook lists maximum Move Over fines of 500 dollars for a first offense, one thousand for a second and two thousand for a third or later offense. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec12-R22 | anchor: A06
A Move Over conviction adds two points to the driver record. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec12-R23 | anchor: A06
Leave generous space behind horse-drawn traffic because it may roll back and its driver may have trouble seeing a close follower. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec12-R24 | anchor: A06
Pass horses or horse-drawn vehicles without excessive speed or horn use, and leave room before returning right to avoid frightening the animal. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec12-R25 | anchor: A07
Follow snowplows from a safe distance because their rear visibility is limited and they spread material that can damage nearby vehicles. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec12-R26 | anchor: A07
Do not attempt to pass a snowplow on either side because wing plows can extend beyond it. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec12-R27 | anchor: A07
Do not retaliate against or try to teach a lesson to another driver after a perceived aggressive act. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec12-R28 | anchor: A07
Let an aggressive driver pass, avoid blocking the passing lane and do not accelerate to challenge the driver. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec12-R29 | anchor: A07
Avoid eye contact and ignore hostile gestures without gesturing back. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec12-R30 | anchor: A07
If safely possible with a hands-free device, call police or 911 about an aggressive driver, or ask a passenger to call. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec12-R31 | anchor: A07
If pursued by an aggressive driver, go to a police station, store or another place with help and witnesses rather than home. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec12-R32 | anchor: A07
When choosing braking or steering to avoid a collision, steering is usually preferable if feasible, especially above 25 mph. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0064]
